sds_facts.storage: Store at 2–8°C (refrigerator). Tightly closed. Dry. Keep in a well-ventilated place. Keep locked up or in an area accessible only to qualified or authorized persons.

bench_knowledge.because: Hygroscopic and deliquescent solids absorb atmospheric water during each weighing event. Mass gain directly dilutes the effective molarity of the solution you prepare. Deliquescent solids (e.g., NaOH pellets) can become partially-dissolved slush within minutes in humid air, further confounding accurate weighing. Desiccator storage and fast weighing are the only controls for this.
bench_knowledge.cite: Sigma-Aldrich Handling Hygroscopic Compounds Technical Note. ASHP Guidelines on Handling Hazardous Drugs (weighing-by-difference rationale).

bench_knowledge.because: Concentrated corrosive reagents (HCl, TFA, NaOH) release significant heat on dilution. Adding water to a concentrated corrosive can boil the liquid and cause spattering; always add the corrosive slowly to water. TFA and HCl volatilise in the hood — decant and dilute in a ventilated space. Waste handling is institution-specific: neutralisation is appropriate only for small compatible corrosive waste streams when performed by trained personnel with the right PPE; otherwise collect through the hazardous-waste program.
bench_knowledge.cite: Sigma-Aldrich HCl Safety Note 258148. ACS Safety in Academic Chemistry Laboratories, 7th ed., Ch. 4. EPA 40 CFR Part 261 (hazardous waste neutralisation).

bench_knowledge.because: The SDS (Section 7 or 8) specifies ventilation controls or fume hood use for this reagent. This category spans volatile toxic solvents (pyridine, DMF, heptane), cytotoxic and genotoxic compounds (docetaxel, streptozocin, azoxymethane), and reagents whose vapours or aerosols pose an inhalation hazard. A chemical fume hood provides the primary engineering control — never handle these reagents on the open bench.
bench_knowledge.cite: OSHA Laboratory Standard 29 CFR 1910.1450. Manufacturer SDS Section 7/8.

bench_knowledge.because: Flammable liquids (flash point < 60°C) generate ignitable vapours at or near room temperature. NFPA 30 and OSHA 29 CFR 1910.106 require storage in FM-approved flammable liquid storage cabinets whenever quantities exceed the exempt amount in standard laboratory containers. Class IB/IC solvents (heptane fp −4°C, ethyl acetate fp −4°C, pyridine fp 20°C) have vapour densities > 1 and will pool at floor level near ignition sources such as hot plates and electrical outlets. Hood use is governed by volatility, toxicity, open-container volume, and SDS ventilation language; the flammable flag alone is enough to require storage and ignition-source controls, but not enough to make every small transfer a hood-only operation.
bench_knowledge.cite: NFPA 30: Flammable and Combustible Liquids Code (2021). OSHA 29 CFR 1910.106 (flammable liquids storage).

bench_knowledge.because: Air-sensitive reagents deteriorate on contact with atmospheric oxygen or moisture. Linoleic acid oxidises to cytotoxic lipid peroxides within hours in open air. Rifampicin degrades to the inactive 3-formyl-rifamycin SV quinone on oxidation. Histamine autooxidises at alkaline pH and is also hygroscopic. DMF absorbs moisture and slowly hydrolyses to dimethylamine (an irritant). Keep bottles tightly capped between uses; aliquot into single-use volumes for high-frequency access. For oxygen-critical applications, consider dispensing under argon.
bench_knowledge.cite: Sigma-Aldrich product information: linoleic acid L1376, rifampicin R3501, DMF D4551. SDS Section 7.
